newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hospital says 130 Palestinians hurt in protest.
newsitem.headline: Hospital says 130 Palestinians hurt in protest.

text.p: Israeli troops wounded 130 Palestinians, five seriously, when they dispersed stone-throwers on Wednesday near Ramallah in the West Bank, a Palestinian hospital director said.

Shawqi Harb, director of Ramallah hospital, said most of the Palestinians treated by his staff had wounds from rubber bullets although one was wounded by gunfire from an M-16 rifle and some suffered from teargas inhalation and beatings.
"Until now we have treated 130, mostly from rubber bullet wounds. This number is changing fast. We have just admitted someone wounded by an M-16," Harb told Reuters.
"It's a fluent situation. Five are in critical condition. They are in surgery now," he said. "I think we will be getting more wounded by the M-16."

Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority had called on Palestinians in Jerusalem and across the West Bank and Gaza to demonstrate against Israel's opening of a tunnel near an Islamic shrine in Jerusalem's walled Old City.
Palestinians answered the call and largely observed a commercial strike.
